write_clauses.syntax: CREATE NODE variable:TypeName { key = value, ... }; | CREATE NODE [ ...batch... ];
write_clauses.description: Creates new node entities. Node-level constraints and default values are evaluated before creation. Batch form factors out the keyword.

batch_syntax.description: Atomic creation of multiple nodes. Implicitly wrapped in a transaction.

write_clauses.validation: Evaluates all node constraints. Fails with [3011] if any constraint is violated. v0.18 enforces [3015] if a required field with no default is omitted.
write_clauses.example: CREATE NODE alice:Person { id = UUID(), name = "Alice", age = 25 };
write_clauses.notes: Constraint validation occurs before commit, within the transaction boundary

write_clauses.syntax: CREATE EDGE variable:TypeName { field = value, role => node, ... }; | CREATE EDGE [ ...batch... ];
write_clauses.description: Creates new hyperedges. Supports batch block syntax. Role binding uses '=>' to assign specific nodes to roles. Validates cardinality, role constraints, and edge constraints before creation.

batch_syntax.syntax: CREATE EDGE [ e1:Type { role => n1 }, e2:Type { role => n2 } ];

binding_operator.purpose: Binds a node instance to a role
binding_operator.distinction: Differs from schema arrows (<- ->) which define directionality

validation.order: 1. Validate nodes exist, 2. Validate cardinality bounds (v0.18), 3. Validate role constraints, 4. Validate edge constraints
validation.error_codes: [3014] for cardinality violations, [3012] for role constraint violations, [3013] for edge constraint violations

write_clauses.example: CREATE EDGE m:Marriage { husband => doug, wife => nini, date = DATE("1999/08/20") };
write_clauses.notes: All role assignments must be valid before edge constraints are evaluated

write_clauses.description: Cross-type atomic creation with shared variable scope. Variables bound in the NODE sub-block are in scope for the EDGE sub-block within the same statement.
write_clauses.atomicity: The entire statement is atomic (all-or-nothing). Error in any entry rolls back the entire batch.
write_clauses.example: CREATE [ NODE [ lucy:Person { ... }, nova:Dog { ... } ], EDGE [ dmn:Owns { owner => lucy, pet => nova } ] ];

write_clauses.syntax: MERGE (var: TypeName { role => node, ... }) [ON CREATE SET ...] [ON MATCH SET ...]
write_clauses.description: Upsert operation. Supports Property-Based Matching OR Role-Binding Matching (if @unique constraint exists on roles). Uses '=>' for role binding.
write_clauses.v018_semantics: DEFAULT values apply ONLY on the ON CREATE path. They are not re-applied to existing records on ON MATCH.
examples:
-- Role-Based (requires @unique(student, course))
MERGE (e:Enrollment { student => s, course => c });

role_binding.description: To MERGE on hyperedge roles, the roles must be part of a @unique constraint. Falls back to property matching if no such constraint exists.

readonly_fields.on_create: Can set @readonly fields - allowed on creation
readonly_fields.example: MERGE (p:Person { email = $email }) ON CREATE SET p.id = UUID(), p.created = NOW() ON MATCH SET p.updated = NOW();

computed_fields.behavior: @computed fields cannot be set via MERGE
computed_fields.workaround: Set underlying fields that computed property depends on

unique_violations.on_create: If ON CREATE SET causes @unique violation, error [3001]
unique_violations.example: MERGE (p:Person { id = $id }) ON CREATE SET p.email = $email -- Fails if email exists

null_in_pattern.behavior: Null in MERGE pattern acts as wildcard, matches any value
null_in_pattern.example: MERGE (p:Person { email = $email, middle_name = null }) -- Matches any Person with that email, regardless of middle_name

role_based_without_unique.example: MERGE (e:Enrollment { student => s, course => c }) -- Fails unless @unique(student, course) exists

write_clauses.description: Bulk property update. Merges provided properties into node/edge, preserving unmentioned fields. Alias for MERGE OBJECT syntax.
write_clauses.semantics: Soft update - only specified fields are modified
write_clauses.example: MATCH (p:Person { id = $id }) SET p += { active = true, last_updated = NOW() };
write_clauses.equivalence: SET p += {...} is equivalent to MERGE OBJECT p WITH {...}
notes: Null values in update object set field to null (not treated as wildcards like in MERGE patterns)
Triggers validation for updated fields only

write_clauses.syntax: SET variable.role += node | SET variable.role += [node1, node2]
write_clauses.description: Atomic Append. Adds node(s) to a role collection.
write_clauses.enforcement: v0.18 enforces cardinality bounds on SET mutations. Triggers [3014] Role Cardinality Violated if count exceeds declared maximum (e.g. attendee <- (10..500)).

write_clauses.description: Atomic Remove. Removes node(s) from a role collection.
write_clauses.enforcement: v0.18 enforces cardinality bounds on SET mutations. Triggers [3014] Role Cardinality Violated if count drops below declared minimum.

write_clauses.syntax: SET variable.field = value | SET variable.role = [n1, n2]
write_clauses.description: Updates specific properties or fully replaces a role collection. Setting a (0..1) role to null is equivalent to removing the binding.
Deletes a node or edge. Fails if connected.

fat_arrow.meaning: Binds node to role (CREATE/MERGE) or filters by existing binding (MATCH)

arrow_operator_summary.design_rationale: Visual distinction between schema (<- ->) and instance (=>) prevents ambiguity.

read_clauses.syntax: IMPORT Name.Space; | IMPORT SCHEMA Name FROM Name.Space; | IMPORT "Path" AS Alias
read_clauses.description: Imports namespaces or named schema units. v0.18 supports dot-hierarchy namespaces.
Matches nodes and edges. Supports inline property predicates for both nodes and edges.

role_match_pattern.description: { role => node } is valid inline filter syntax within a MATCH pattern object. Role bindings (=>) and property filters (:) may coexist in the same pattern object.
role_match_pattern.rationale: Hyperedges are first-class entities and must be retrievable by role binding with the same expressiveness as nodes are retrievable by property filter.

edge_property_matching.description: Edge properties can be filtered inline in the pattern
edge_property_matching.equivalence: Inline edge properties are equivalent to WHERE clause filters but may enable better query optimization

syntax_enforcement.note: '=' is strictly prohibited inside a MATCH pattern object. ':' is the only valid delimiter for inline property filters in MATCH. '=' is reserved for assignment in write contexts (CREATE, SET).

block_syntax.description: Patterns in the block are resolved together as a join.
block_syntax.modifier: OPTIONAL keyword becomes a per-pattern modifier inside the block, replacing the legacy standalone clause form.

read_clauses.syntax: MATCH PATH var = (start)-[:Edge* {role} WEIGHT BY field USING [SUM|MAX|MIN|AVG]]->(end)

read_clauses.description: Matches pattern or returns nulls. Standalone clause remains valid for backward compatibility.
Filters matched results. Supports block syntax.

block_syntax.description: Entries in the block are implicitly ANDed together.

read_clauses.syntax: WHERE ALL|ANY|NONE(var IN path.nodes|path.edges WHERE condition)
field IS NULL | field IS NOT NULL
string LIKE pattern | string ILIKE pattern
string MATCHES regex | string IMATCHES regex

block_syntax.syntax: WITH [ p, COLLECT(f.name) AS friends, COUNT(f) AS friend_count ];

read_clauses.syntax: RETURN var | expression [AS alias] | { field: expr, ... } [AS alias] | var { field1, field2, ... } [AS alias] | [ field: expr, ... ]
read_clauses.description: Final projection. Supports block syntax for structured output.

block_syntax.syntax: RETURN [ name: p.name, friends: friends, rank: RANK() OVER (ORDER BY p.age DESC) ];
block_syntax.note: Block form is appropriate for 3+ entries to improve scanability.

nested.example: RETURN { person: p { name, age }, company: c { name } }

examples: RETURN { person: p { name }, friends: COLLECT(f { name }) }

read_clauses.description: Combines results from two queries, keeping duplicates. Queries must return compatible types.
read_clauses.example: MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n UNION ALL MATCH (m:Person) RETURN m;

query_parameters.description: HyperQL supports parameterized queries for security, performance, and query plan caching.

syntax.description: Parameters use $ prefix followed by identifier. Case-sensitive.

type_binding.description: Parameter types are inferred from context on first use. Subsequent uses must match the inferred type.

usage_contexts.example: CREATE EDGE m:Marriage { date: $wedding_date, husband => $h, wife => $w }

query_preparation.support: Queries with parameters can be prepared and cached
query_preparation.syntax: PREPARE stmt AS MATCH (p:Person { id: $id }) RETURN p;

null_handling.behavior: Null parameter values are allowed for nullable fields

whitespace_free_readability_guarantee: All v0.18 block syntax forms are unambiguous even if all whitespace is removed, enabled by balanced delimiters ([, ] and {, }).

introspection.description: Lists all User-Defined Functions in the current namespace.
Shows the signature and body of a specific function.

introspection.syntax: VALIDATE CONSTRAINT Type.ConstraintName WITH { field: value };
introspection.description: Dry-run validation of a constraint against hypothetical data.
Shows query execution plan without running the query

default.output: Human-readable text format showing plan tree

introspection.example: EXPLAIN VERBOSE MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.age > 30 RETURN p;

introspection.description: Executes query and shows actual execution statistics alongside plan

default.output: Plan with actual row counts and timing

verbose.output: Detailed execution statistics including cache hits, I/O operations

introspection.description: Returns the execution plan and interpreter cost estimate for a function.
Returns the AST and execution plan for a constraint.

constraint_limits.description: Operational limits to prevent abuse and ensure stability.

udf_limits.description: Interpreter safety limits to prevent infinite loops and stack overflows.
